settings.introHTML: This lesson teaches learners how to describe different types of housing and rooms in French, using vocabulary for household spaces and furnishings. It introduces the expression il y a (there is / are) and verbs used only in the third person (for example il pleut, il faut), while reinforcing adjectival agreement patterns such as spacieux / spacieuse. It also develops pronunciation through the nasal vowel sound an (as in blanc, chambre), helping learners speak more naturally when describing their home and surroundings.
settings.informationHTML:
After completing this unit, you will be able to:

  • Describe different types of housing, rooms, and household spaces in French.
  • Use il y a to say what there is or what a home contains.
  • Recognise and use common home-related vocabulary, including floor and room names.
  • Apply adjectival agreement more accurately with forms such as spacieux / spacieuse and related patterns.
  • Recognise and produce the French nasal vowel sound an in common words linked to home and everyday life.

monologues.informationTextHTML: This section introduces short monologues that describe where people live and what their homes are like in French.

phraseTable1.informationTextHTML: Read each phrase, then play its audio clip to check pronunciation and meaning.
phrases: J'habite dans un appartement au premier étage d'un grand immeuble.  J'ai une petite cuisine et une salle de séjour et un petit balcon aussi. Ma chambre n'est pas grande, mais elle est confortable. Derrière l'immeuble, il y a un jardin communautaire.

I live in a flat on the first floor of a large block of flats. I've got a small kitchen, a living room and a small balcony as well. My bedroom isn't big, but it's comfortable. Behind the block of flats there's a communal garden.

Cette année, je loue une maison.  Elle est petite. Au rez-de-chaussée, il y a la cuisine et la salle de séjour. A l'étage, il y a deux chambres, une pour moi et une autre pour mes invités. La salle de bains et les toilettes se trouvent à l'étage aussi.

This year I'm renting a house. It's small. On the ground floor there's the kitchen and the living room. Upstairs there are two bedrooms, one for me and another one for my guests. The bathroom and toilet are upstairs too.

Mes parents ont une grande maison à la campagne.  Au rez-de-chaussée, il y a une grande cuisine et une buanderie ainsi qu'un salon et une salle à manger et une petite salle de séjour. Ils n'ont pas de bureau.  Au premier étage, il y a une salle de bains, des toilettes, une douche et quatre chambres. Ils ont une cave aussi où ils mettent leur vin !

My parents have a big house in the countryside. On the ground floor there's a big kitchen, a utility room as well as a lounge and a dining room and a small living room. They don't have a study. On the first floor there's a bathroom, a toilet, a shower room and four bedrooms. They've also got a cellar where they put their wine!

vocabulary.informationTextHTML: This section introduces the key housing, room, and descriptive vocabulary used in the unit.

You will learn:

  • Core housing and room vocabulary (for example logement, chambre, cuisine, balcon).
  • Useful location expressions within a home (for example au rez-de-chaussée, à l'étage, au sous-sol).
  • Adjectives used to describe homes and rooms (for example confortable, spacieux / spacieuse, lumineux / lumineuse).
  • Vocabulary that supports description, listening, and speaking tasks about home and accommodation.
phrases: on the first / second / third floor

toilettesNote.informationTextHTML: In France the plural form is used even if there is just one facility. In other francophone countries, the singular la toilette occurs.

grammar1.informationTextHTML:
In this section, you will learn how French uses il in fixed expressions and impersonal verbs.

You will learn:

  • How il y a is used to say what there is or what a place contains.
  • How verbs such as pleuvoir, neiger, and falloir are used in the third person singular.
  • How these forms help you describe homes and everyday situations more naturally.
grammar1.titleTextHTML: 1. Il y a and other third-person forms

grammar2.informationTextHTML:
This section introduces some new adjectives.

You will learn:

  • How adjectives ending in -eux behave in masculine and feminine forms.
  • How to recognise the feminine singular ending -euse.
  • How agreement changes in singular and plural examples used to describe rooms and homes.

instructionsLayout.paragraphHTML: This section introduces key grammar and usage for describing homes and rooms in French, with a focus on il y a, third-person-only verbs, and adjective agreement.

pronunciation1.informationTextHTML: In this part, focus on the French nasal sound an. Listen to each model, repeat aloud, and notice how the sound is formed in common words.

pronunciation2.informationTextHTML: Here, expand recognition of the same nasal sound across related spellings such as an, am, en, and em. Listen, compare, and repeat each example carefully.

items.text: J'habite [seule]. Mon appartement n'est pas [très] grand, mais il est très [confortable].  Il y a [une] salle de séjour [lumineuse]. Elle [est] très jolie. J'ai un petit [balcon] – c'est super !  Il y a [deux] chambres, une pour [moi] et une autre [petite] chambre pour mes invités. J'ai une salle de bains et des [toilettes], bien sûr ! Il y a [un] jardin devant l'immeuble.

instructionsLayout.paragraphHTML: This section gives you a chance to practise the key points from this unit. You will check your vocabulary for rooms and household items along with the correct gender and adjective agreement, apply il y a in everyday descriptions, and complete short listening and gap-fill tasks about French homes.
